body:
Prompt injection risk: content/content.js decodes and normalizes untrusted JSON-LD JobPosting.description text (stripLdHtml) which can include attacker-controlled instructions; that description is later interpolated into Gemini prompts (e.g., background/modules/handlers/interview.js buildInterviewQuestionsPrompt uses job.description, and lib/gemini.js generateAnswers uses jd). There is no robust control to force the model to treat the JD as data-only (e.g., strict instruction + clear delimiting / quoting), so a crafted job page can steer outputs and potentially cause resume/profile details (included elsewhere in prompts) to be echoed or misused. --- General fix: when untrusted page text is later sent to an LLM, transform it into a clearly delimited **data payload** and add local hardening to reduce instruction-like content from being interpreted as control text. Since we are constrained to content/content.js, the best fix here is to sanitize/neutralize common instruction markers before this text is passed downstream.

Best single-file fix (without changing core functionality): update stripLdHtml to:

  • correctly decode named entities (&, <, >, ", ',  );
  • remove control characters;
  • neutralize prompt-injection framing tokens (triple backticks, XML-like instruction tags, role markers such as system:, assistant:, user:, and imperative “ignore previous instructions” patterns);
  • keep output as readable plain text and preserve truncation behavior already done by caller.

This should be done in content/content.js in the stripLdHtml function region (lines 576–594 shown).
